acceptOwnership().details: The new owner accepts the ownership transfer.

params.initialOwner: Owner (the production timelock) — sets caps and        the operator roster.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

setOperators(address[],uint8).details: Does NOT reset an active halt or already-cast votes (see the         contract-level roster-change note).

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner. Setting `newOwner` to the zero address is allowed; this can be used to cancel an initiated ownership transfer.

HALT_DURATION().notice: E2 halt auto-expiry: a halt lapses after this unless a quorum         extends it (no indefinite single-operator freeze).

REHALT_COOLDOWN().notice: Per-operator re-halt cooldown measured from the operator's         previous `halt()`: 48h = the 24h halt + 24h quiet, so one         rogue operator cannot chain-freeze; a SUSTAINED freeze needs         either a quorum (governance) or ≥2 colluding operators.

TIGHTEN_COOLDOWN().notice: Per-operator cooldown on the emergency tighten path.

checkAttest(bytes32,uint256).notice: Meters a mint attested-credit against the OM-4 window. Caller         MUST be the intent queue. NOT halt-gated: blocking in-flight         credit recording during a halt would push honest in-flight         mints past their deadline into cancel + swap-back (itself a         custody spend); the attest window + the price-oracle deviation         breaker still bound the credit rate during an incident.

checkDispatch(bytes32[],uint256[]).notice: Meters a redemption's leg dispatches against the E1 outflow         windows and enforces the halt — one atomic call per         redemption. Caller MUST be the intent queue. Reverts         {CustodyGuard_Halted} while halted (a halt blocks new outflow         commitments), {CustodyGuard_DispatchCapExceeded} when any         leg's window cap would be exceeded (the whole redemption         reverts), {CustodyGuard_LengthMismatch} on ragged arrays. A         `0` cap disables metering for that asset (the halt check         still applies). Multiple legs of one asset accumulate within         the call.

dispatchWindow(bytes32).notice: Current-bucket dispatch window, normalized: a stale stored         bucket reads as `used = 0` for the current bucket.

halt().notice: Halts custody-lifecycle starts for {haltDuration}. Any single         operator (fail-closed; DL-CTD-E). Reverts while already halted         and during the caller's re-halt cooldown.

haltedUntil().notice: The active halt's expiry (or a past timestamp when not halted).

intentQueue().notice: The intent queue authorized to consume window capacity. Also         the back-pointer `IntentQueue.setCustodyGuard` validates.

isHalted().notice: True while a halt is active (`block.timestamp < haltedUntil`).

nextHaltAllowedAt(address).notice: The caller's earliest next allowed `halt()` timestamp.

nextTightenAllowedAt(address).notice: The caller's earliest next allowed tighten timestamp.

quorum().notice: Votes required to un-halt or extend (3 in the production         3-of-5 deployment).

renounceOwnership().notice: Permanently disabled — losing the owner would brick cap and         roster governance (same posture as the queue / oracle, S-2).

requireNotHalted().notice: Reverts {CustodyGuard_Halted} while a halt is active. Consumed         by `IntentQueue.createMintIntent` (new mint lifecycles are         fail-closed during an incident) and observer tooling.

setOperators(address[],uint8).notice: Replaces the operator roster and quorum. Owner-only (timelock         at production — roster rotation is a governed ceremony).

setVolumeCaps(bytes32,uint256,uint256).notice: Sets both caps for an asset. Owner-only; `0` disables that         side. At production the owner is the timelock, so RAISES         inherit the timelock delay (DL-CTD-E); instant tightening is         the operator path ({tightenDispatchCap}).

tightenDispatchCap(bytes32,uint256).notice: Operator emergency instant-tighten of an asset's dispatch cap         (floored at `currentCap / 5` per call, per-operator cooldown).         Raising caps is owner-only ({CustodyGuard_CapNotTightening}).

voteExtendHalt().notice: Votes to extend the active halt by one more {haltDuration};         executes at quorum. Each extension is a fresh vote round.

voteUnhalt().notice: Votes to end the active halt early; executes at quorum.

@title CustodyGuard
 @notice CTD-1 Slice E containment (DL-CTD-E): E1 per-asset volume
         circuit-breaker + E2 operator halt — see {ICustodyGuard}.
 @dev   Holds no funds. Pure accounting + roster state consumed by the
        `IntentQueue` hooks; makes no external calls, so there is no
        reentrancy surface. The owner is the production timelock (M-A2),
        so cap raises and roster changes inherit the timelock delay; the
        instant paths are deliberately the OPERATOR powers (halt, floored
        tighten) — fail-closed-only levers.
        Roster-change edge (documented, accepted): replacing operators
        mid-halt neither resets the halt nor un-counts votes already cast
        for the current halt nonce/round. Roster rotation is a
        timelock-governed ceremony; an emergency roster change during an
        active incident is operationally out of scope.
